page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.4xlarge is an enhanced general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via KVM, the configuration delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation stands at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU subsystem features a 48 MB L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark measurements position the instance squarely in the middle 50% across compute, memory, and application-level workloads. CPU benchmarks report a PassMark CPU score of 20,920.78, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,721.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 15,531.53. Memory throughput shows substantial read and write capabilities, measuring 97.84 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 57.96 GB/sec for uncached writes. Application-layer benchmarks reflect steady enterprise performance, demonstrating 15.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.98 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on remote block storage for persistence. Network connectivity is provisioned with a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. In terms of cost efficiency, its standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory profile offers a balanced distribution of resources without paying for specialized acceleration hardware or excessive RAM capacity.

Given its consistent mid-range compute scores and standard memory density, Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.4xlarge is suited for standard enterprise production workloads. These include mid-tier relational databases, in-memory caching clusters such as Redis, static and dynamic web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and lightweight CPU-based inference for smaller machine learning models.
